explanation: Build rows in increasing order. Set each endpoint to one and each interior entry to the sum of its two parents in the completed previous row.
timeComplexity: O(n²+1): the output has 1+2+…+n=n(n+1)/2 entries, each initialized and computed a constant number of times.
spaceComplexity: O(n²+1) returned triangle storage. Rows being filled become part of the output; loop indices use O(1) extra state.
attribution: Original C# implementation and explanation authored for EPI Practice from the displayed problem contract.
correctness: Row zero is [1]. Assuming the previous row is correct, each endpoint of the next row is one and each interior position equals the sum of its two parents, exactly Pascal’s recurrence. Induction on row number proves every generated row correct. Returning all n rows includes each requested coefficient once.
walkthrough: For n=4, begin [1] and [1,1]. The next row has middle value 1+1=2, giving [1,2,1]. Its two parent sums are 1+2=3 and 2+1=3, giving [1,3,3,1]. Return [[1],[1,1],[1,2,1],[1,3,3,1]].
edgeCases: The bank uses 0≤n≤34, so all coefficients fit signed 32-bit integers.
